```{r}
#| context: setup
#| include: false

#Get Global Functions
#Note; this won't work properly on HH data
#Replaces the NEE_VUT_REF values with NA when their QC is less than a threshold
filter_fluxes <- function(flux_df, QC_threshold){
  indexes_to_filter <- flux_df$NEE_VUT_REF_QC < QC_threshold
  flux_df$NEE_VUT_REF <- replace(flux_df$NEE_VUT_REF, indexes_to_filter, NA)
  return(flux_df)
}

filter_variables <- function(flux_df, QC_threshold,variables){
  for (variable in variables){
    if (substr(variable ,1,3) == "GPP" | substr(variable ,1,4) == "RECO"){
      #GPP and RECO don't have their own quality flags they just use the NEE one
      indexes_to_filter <- flux_df[,"NEE_VUT_REF_QC"] < QC_threshold
      flux_df[, variable] <- replace(flux_df[,variable], indexes_to_filter, NA)
    } else {
      indexes_to_filter <- flux_df[,paste(variable, "QC", sep = "_")] < QC_threshold
      flux_df[, variable] <- replace(flux_df[,variable], indexes_to_filter, NA)
    }
  }
  return(flux_df)
}

```



```{r}
#Set up UI

available_variables <- c("Temperature", "Shortwave Radiation", "Net Radiation", "Vapor Pressure Deficit", 
                         "Precipitation", "Evapotranspiration", "PPFD")

available_Yvariables <- c("NEE", "GPP", "RECO")


available_sites <- c("1850 Burn", "1930 Burn", "1964 Burn (dry)", "1964 Burn (wet)", "1981 Burn", "1989 Burn", "1998 Burn")

available_timescales <- c("Daily", "Weekly", "Monthly")

available_statistics <- c("Min", "Max", "Mean", "STD", "Min Day of Year", "Max Day of Year", "Relational Correlation", 
                          "Relational Single Regression Slope", "Relational Multiple Regression Slope", 
                          "Relational Nearest Neighbor RSS")

tabsetPanel(
  tabPanel("Variable vs Flux By Site", 
            card(card_body(
                "
                These plots allow you to investigate the relationship between a variable of your choice and NEE, GPP, or RECO
                at your desired timescale (default weekly) in scatterplot form. You can choose which site you want to display 
                in each of the two panels to do a side by side comparison. The nearest-neighbor smoothing averages of the 
                relationship between all sites is also shown.
                "
            )),
            layout_sidebar(
              sidebar = sidebarPanel(
                accordion(
                  open = c("Variables"),
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Variables",
                    radioButtons("chosenVariable", "Environmental Variable", available_variables, selected = "Temperature"),
                    radioButtons("chosenYVariable", "Flux Variable", available_Yvariables, selected = "NEE")
                  ),
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Site 1",
                    radioButtons("chosenSite1", "Site 1:", available_sites, selected = "1850 Burn")
                  ), 
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Site 2",
                    radioButtons("chosenSite2", "Site 2:", available_sites, selected = "1998 Burn")
                  ),
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Timescales",
                    radioButtons("chosenTimescale", "Temporal Resolution:", available_timescales, selected = "Weekly")
                  ))),
              accordion(
                accordion_panel(
                  "Comparative Site Scatterplots",
                  layout_columns(
                      plotOutput("Site1VarNEEScatterplot"),
                      plotOutput("Site2VarNEEScatterplot")
                )),
                accordion_panel(
                  "All Site Splines",
                  plotOutput("VarNEESplineplot")
                )
              ))),
  tabPanel("Variable Stats By Years Since Burn",
             card(card_body(
                "
                This plot allows you to investigate the relationship between some common stats about an investigated variable and the
                number of years since burn. These stats include the min, max, mean, and standard deviation of a single variable
                (daily scale) and the day of the year at which a given variable was highest or lowest. This also allows you to
                look at stats about the relationship between a given variable and a flux variable; including the R^2 of the
                correlation between the investigated and relational (flux) variable, the slope of the regression line between the predictor and
                the flux variable (either single or multiple), and the RSS of the nearest neighbor regression line displayed in
                the Variable vs Flux by Site (a measure of how predictable flux is from that variable); all at the daily scale.
                "
            )),
            layout_sidebar(
              sidebar = sidebarPanel(
                accordion(
                  open = c("Stat Choice", "Variables"),
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Stat Choice",
                    radioButtons("chosenStat", "Statistic to Plot", available_statistics,
                                 selected = "Min")),
                  accordion_panel(
                    "Variables",
                    radioButtons("chosenVariable2", "Investigated Variable", append(available_variables, available_Yvariables),
                                 selected = "Temperature"),
                    radioButtons("chosenYVariable2", "Relational Variable", available_Yvariables, selected = "NEE")
                  ))),
              plotOutput("StatPlot")
            ))
)
```



Note: I'm using the nighttime partitioning method for GPP
```{r}
#| context: server

variables_names_to_ids <- c("Temperature" = "TA_F", "Shortwave Radiation" = "SW_IN_F", "Longwave Radiation" = "LW_IN_F",
                            "Net Radiation" = "NETRAD", "Vapor Pressure Deficit" = "VPD_F", "Pressure" = "PA_F", 
                            "Precipitation" = "P_F", "Wind Speed" = "WS_F", "Evapotranspiration" = "ET", "PPFD" = "PPFD_IN",
                            "NEE" = "NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP" = "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO" = "RECO_NT_VUT_REF")



sites_names_to_ids <- c("1850 Burn" = "CA-NS1", "1930 Burn" = "CA-NS2", "1964 Burn (dry)" = "CA-NS3", 
                        "1964 Burn (wet)" = "CA-NS4", "1981 Burn" = "CA-NS5", "1989 Burn" = "CA-NS6", "1998 Burn" = "CA-NS7")


sites_ids_to_names <- c("CA-NS1" = "1850 Burn", "CA-NS2" = "1930 Burn", "CA-NS3" = "1964 Burn (dry)", 
                        "CA-NS4" = "1964 Burn (wet)", "CA-NS5" = "1981 Burn", "CA-NS6" = "1989 Burn", "CA-NS7" = "1998 Burn")


filtering_threshold <- 0.8

site_colors <- c("CA-NS1" = "#f92104", "CA-NS2" = "#f9a600", "CA-NS3" = "#2df900", "CA-NS4" = "#00f9f9", 
                 "CA-NS5" = "#0031f9", "CA-NS6" = "#9202f9", "CA-NS7" = "#f902d8")

data <- reactive({
  if (input$chosenTimescale == "Weekly"){
    data <- WW_data
  } else if (input$chosenTimescale == "Daily"){
    data <- DD_data
  } else {
    data <- MM_data
  }
  return(data)
})

Xscale <- reactive({
  data <- data()
  variable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenVariable]
  min_val <- min(data$variable_id)
  max_val <- max(data$variable_id)
  range_val <- range(data$variable_id)[1] - range(data$variable_id)[2] 
  c(min_val - 0.1*range_val, max_val + .1*range_val)
})

Yscale <- reactive({
  data <- data()
  yval <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenYVariable]
  min_val <- min(data$yval)
  max_val <- max(data$yval)
  range_val <- range(data$yval)[1] - range(data$yval)[2] 
  c(min_val - 0.1*range_val, max_val + .1*range_val)
})

output$Site1VarNEEScatterplot <- renderPlot({
  
  variable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenVariable]
  Yvariable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenYVariable]
  site_id = sites_names_to_ids[input$chosenSite1]
  
  
  siteData <- data() 
  siteData <- siteData |> filter(Site == site_id) |> 
                       filter_variables(0.8, c(Yvariable_id, variable_id))
  
  xlims <- Xscale()
  ylims <- Yscale()
  
  siteData |> ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(variable_id), y = !!sym(Yvariable_id))) +
            xlim(xlims[1],xlims[2]) + ylim(ylims[1],ylims[2]) +
            geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = site_colors[site_id]) + 
            geom_smooth(se = T, color = "black") + scale_alpha(guide = "none") +
            labs(x = input$chosenVariable, y = input$chosenYVariable, 
                 title = paste("Relationship between", input$chosenVariable, "\n and", input$chosenYVariable ,
                               "at the", input$chosenSite1, "Site")) + theme_classic()
})

output$Site2VarNEEScatterplot <- renderPlot({

  variable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenVariable]
  Yvariable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenYVariable]
  site_id = sites_names_to_ids[input$chosenSite2]
  
  siteData <- data() |> filter(Site == site_id) |> 
                       filter_variables(0.8, c(Yvariable_id, variable_id))
  
  xlims <- Xscale()
  ylims <- Yscale()
  
  siteData |> ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(variable_id), y = !!sym(Yvariable_id))) +
            xlim(xlims[1],xlims[2]) + ylim(ylims[1],ylims[2]) +
            geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = site_colors[site_id]) + 
            geom_smooth(se = T, color = "black") + scale_alpha(guide = "none") +
            labs(x = input$chosenVariable, y = input$chosenYVariable,
                 title = paste("Relationship between", input$chosenVariable, "\n and", input$chosenVariable,
                               "at the", input$chosenSite2, "Site"))  + theme_classic()
})

output$VarNEESplineplot <- renderPlot({

  variable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenVariable]
  Yvariable_id <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenYVariable]
  
  variableData <- data() |> filter_variables(0.8, c(Yvariable_id, variable_id))
  
  xlims <- Xscale()
  ylims <- Yscale()
  
  variableData |> ggplot(aes(x = !!sym(variable_id), y = !!sym(Yvariable_id), color = Site)) +
            xlim(xlims[1],xlims[2]) + ylim(ylims[1],ylims[2]) +
            geom_smooth(se = T, alpha = 0.2) + scale_alpha(guide = "none") +
            scale_color_manual(labels = sites_ids_to_names, values = site_colors) +
            labs(x = input$chosenVariable, y = input$chosenYVariable,
                 title = paste("Relationship between", input$chosenVariable, "and ",input$chosenYVariable," at all sites")) +
            theme_classic()
})
```

```{r}
#| context: server
#| include: FALSE

sites_ids_to_burntime <- c("CA-NS1" = 152, "CA-NS2" = 72, "CA-NS3" = 38, 
                        "CA-NS4" = 38, "CA-NS5" = 21, "CA-NS6" = 13, "CA-NS7" = 2)


available_variables <- c("Temperature", "Shortwave Radiation", "Net Radiation", "Vapor Pressure Deficit", 
                         "Precipitation", "Evapotranspiration", "PPFD")

get_stats <- reactive({
  
  years_since_burn = rep(0,7)
  min_val = rep(0,7) 
  max_val = rep(0,7)
  mean_val = rep(0,7)
  std_val = rep(0,7)
  min_doy = rep(0,7) 
  max_doy = rep(0,7)
  correlation = rep(0,7)
  single_slope = rep(0,7)
  multiple_slope = rep(0,7)
  loess_RSS = rep(0,7)
  
  Xvar <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenVariable2]
  Yvar <- variables_names_to_ids[input$chosenYVariable2]
  
  index <- 1
  
  for (siteID in sites_names_to_ids) {
    years_since_burn[index] = sites_ids_to_burntime[siteID]
    
    Xdata <- DD_data |> filter(Site == siteID) |> filter_variables(0.8, c(Xvar)) 
    Xdata <- Xdata[, c("TIMESTAMP", Xvar)] |> drop_na()
    days_of_year <- Xdata |> pull(var = TIMESTAMP) |> yday()
    Xdata <- Xdata |> mutate("DOY" = days_of_year)
    
    min_val[index] <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> min()
    max_val[index] <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> max()
    mean_val[index] <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> mean()
    std_val[index] <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> sd()
    
    min_ind <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> which.min()
    min_doy[index] <- Xdata[min_ind, "DOY"] |> deframe()
    max_ind <- Xdata |> pull(var = Xvar) |> which.max()
    max_doy[index] <- Xdata[max_ind, "DOY"] |> deframe()
    
    BothData <-  DD_data |> filter(Site == siteID) |> filter_variables(0.8, c(Xvar, Yvar))
    
    
    if (Xvar == Yvar){
      correlation[index] <- 1
      single_slope[index] <- 1
      multiple_slope[index] <- 1
      loess_RSS[index] <- 0
    } else {
    
      if (Xvar %in% variables_names_to_idso[available_variables]){
       AllData <- DD_data|> filter(Site == siteID) |> filter_variables(0.8, c(variables_names_to_ids[available_variables], Yvar)) 
       AllData <- AllData[,c(variables_names_to_ids[available_variables], Yvar)] |> drop_na()
      } else {
       AllData <- DD_data |> filter(Site == siteID) |> 
         filter_variables(0.8, c(variables_names_to_ids[available_variables], Xvar, Yvar))
       AllData <- AllData[,c(variables_names_to_ids[available_variables], Xvar, Yvar)] |> drop_na()
      }
      
      single_regression <- lm(as.formula(paste(Yvar, "~", Xvar)), data = BothData)
      
      correlation[index] <- summary(single_regression)$r.squared
      single_slope[index] <- summary(single_regression)$coefficients[Xvar, "Estimate"]
      
      
      multiple_regression <- lm(as.formula(paste(Yvar, "~ .")), data = AllData)
      multiple_slope[index] <- summary(multiple_regression)$coefficients[Xvar, "Estimate"]
      
      loess_regression <- loess(as.formula(paste(Yvar, "~", Xvar)), data = BothData)
      loess_RSS[index] <- sum(summary(loess_regression)$residuals ** 2)
      
    }
    index <- index + 1
  }
  df <- tibble("YearsSinceBurn" = years_since_burn, "Min" = min_val, "Max" = max_val, "Mean" = mean_val, "STD" = std_val, 
         "Min Day of Year" = min_doy, "Max Day of Year" = max_doy, "Relational Correlation" = correlation, 
         "Relational Single Regression Slope" = single_slope, "Relational Multiple Regression Slope" = multiple_slope,
         "Relational Nearest Neighbor RSS" = loess_RSS)
  df
})
```

```{r}
#| context: server


stats_to_xlab <- reactive({
  Xvar <- input$chosenVariable2
  Yvar <- input$chosenYVariable2
  c("Min" = paste("Min of", Xvar), "Max" = paste("Max of", Xvar), "Mean" = paste("Mean of", Xvar),
    "STD" = paste("STD of", Xvar), "Min Day of Year" = paste("Day of Year of Min", Xvar), 
    "Max Day of Year"= paste("Day of Year of Max", Xvar), 
    "Relational Correlation" = paste("$R^2$ Between", Xvar, "and", Yvar),
    "Relational Single Regression Slope" = paste("Single Regression Slope of", Yvar, "from", Xvar), 
    "Relational Multiple Regression Slope" = paste("Multiple Regression Slope of", Yvar, "from", Xvar), 
    "Relational Nearest Neighbor RSS" = paste("RSS of Nearest Neighbor Regression of", Yvar, "from", Xvar))
})

output$StatPlot <- renderPlot({
  chosen_stat <- input$chosenStat
  xlabs_dict <- stats_to_xlab()
  stats <- get_stats()
  print(stats)
  stats |> ggplot(aes(x = YearsSinceBurn, y = !!sym(chosen_stat))) + geom_point(size = 5) + xlab("Years Since Burn") + 
    ylab(xlabs_dict[chosen_stat]) + theme_classic()
})
```
